notes:
Account background: mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B). Customers include finance and retail verticals; strict EU & US residency segmentation for PII. Started with Hosted API POC (Dec 2025) -> positive perf results, moved to Dedicated evaluation for predictable unit economics.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-12-09: Initial hosted API POC kickoff. Engineering ran embedding batch jobs and baseline latency tests (avg 45ms/token for short chat calls).
- 2026-01-12: Demo (Fireflies ff_20260112_nb-axon-demo). Walkthrough of routing, cache and canary features. Product team liked prefix caching.
- 2026-02-02: POC results review: embeddings throughput ok, noted 18% cost savings with batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize prototype.
- 2026-02-22: Pricing deep-dive with AE/SE (Fireflies ff_20260222_nb-axon-pricing-call). Discussed Dedicated commit tiers, burst windows and overage policies.
- 2026-03-03: Legal sent initial redlines on MSA (data residency + audit rights). Jira INF-9421 opened for compliance Qs.
- 2026-03-08: Finance asked for committed spend scenarios vs expected token volumes for 12-month term.

Use-case & requirements (as captured in calls):
- Primary workload: real-time product assistants (chat) + nightly rerank/embeddings for search.
- Latency: 95th percentile chat latency target <= 120ms (in-us), embeddings batch throughput target 40k vectors/hour.
- Throughput: steady-state ~120 reqs/s chat during peak; spiky bursts up to 500 reqs/s for launches.
- Cost sensitivity: high — need predictable $/token and committed discounts; overage must be bounded and transparent.
- Models: prefer open Llama-family/equivalent quantized variants for cost; want ability to fallback to smaller models for non-critical traffic.
- Routing/fallback: MUST support policy-based routing by region and tier, auto-fallback to cheaper variant on overload.
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs retention 2 years, KMS integration for customer keys, data residency enforcement per tenant.

Dedicated packaging preferences discussed:
- Target: 12-month Dedicated contract with quarterly ramp schedule. Proposed commit = reserved vGPU-hours equivalent to 2x peak steady-state (approx. 8 A100-equivalent GPU hours/day) to hit latency SLOs.
- Burst: 10% guaranteed burst headroom included, additional burst purchased as hourly burst pool at defined rate. Needs ability to consume short-term burst up to 3x steady capacity for 2-hour windows during product launches.
- Overage: proposal on table = 1.4x committed unit price for on-demand overage; customer requested cap (monthly overage not to exceed 20% of committed spend).
- Ramp schedule: Month1 50% commit, Month2 75%, Month3 100% — Redwood to credit unused commit during first quarter if underutilized.
- Pricing ask from customer: tiered committed discount ladder (5% @ 12k/month, 10% @ 24k/month, 15% @ 48k/month) and predictable per-token equivalent for accounting.

Key quotes / snippets:
- "We like the runtime performance but need deterministic unit economics — spikes kill our margins." (VP Product, 2026-02-22)
- "If Redwood can formalize a ramp + overage cap we can commit to 12 months." (Finance lead, 2026-03-08)

Open items / action items:

- Legal: respond to MSA redlines; confirm data residency enforcement model (expected reply by 2026-03-20).
- SE: finalize benchmark run for 95th pct latency on proposed Dedicated config (A100-equivalent) and share results (target 2026-03-14).
- Finance: provide final ARR approval once illustrative pricing spreadsheet integrated with internal forecasting (customer expects by 2026-03-18).

Next steps (short):

- Anika to schedule on-prem-equivalent perf run with Redwood infra team (3/14).
- Marcus to prepare onboarding/CS plan conditional on signature (kickoff within 2 weeks of contract).
